changes.after: A pipe sends the result on its left into the function call on its right.

before: The native |> pipe normally inserts its left expression as the first argument of the call on the right. This expression is equivalent to sum(c(1, NA, 3), na.rm = TRUE); it is ordinary R syntax, not a package dependency.

To place the value explicitly in a named argument, a named _ placeholder can be used once in an eligible call, such as value |> round(x = _, digits = 1). A pipe does not automatically vectorize a scalar-only function or change its missing-value behavior.

Complete local R example; the app itself does not execute it:
```r
result <- c(1, NA, 3) |> sum(na.rm = TRUE)
cat(result, "\n")
```
